review_scope_note: Unlike prior API-based reviews that saw only the finding text, this audit had full repository access: experiment kernels, archived run logs/CSVs, prior reviews, remediations, and paper/CERTIFICATE.md where applicable. Quantitative claims were checked against primary artifacts; arithmetic and hashes were recomputed where feasible. No computational result was invented.
verification_methods: Independently re-read run_10B_v2.log, run_10B_v3.log, run_100B.log, run_100B_v2.log, run_210B.log tails
Confirmed silent clipping path and mark-before-drop order in matrix_enum_multipass.cu
Confirmed zaremba_verify_v4.c is single-threaded with no OpenMP
Cross-checked paper/CERTIFICATE.md clipping audit and frontier probes
Compared finding text against the 2026-07-21 claude-fable-5 deep audit and re-verified its decisive claims

claim_reviews.claim: Every bounded CF path corresponds to a product of matrices g_a=[[a,1],[1,0]]; enumerating Zaremba denominators is equivalent to batched 2x2 matrix products.
claim_reviews.evidence: Classical continuant/SL(2) correspondence; kernels initialize exactly these generators and use the convergent recurrence n10 = m10*a + m11.

claim_reviews.claim: The fused expand+mark+compact CUDA kernel exists as described.
claim_reviews.evidence: matrix_enum.cu (v5) and matrix_enum_multipass.cu (v6) implement fused expansion, atomicOr bitset marking, atomicAdd compaction, and double buffering.
claim_reviews.concerns: Silent drop when pos >= max_out is omitted from the finding; marks fire before the drop, so Uncovered:0 remains one-sidedly sound but clipped runs do less work.

claim_reviews.claim: 175x speedup at 1e7: v4 CPU tree-walk 157s on 2x Xeon (224 threads, OpenMP) vs 0.9s for v5 on one B200.
claim_reviews.evidence: 157/0.9=174.4 is arithmetically consistent, but neither timing is archived. Committed zaremba_verify_v4.c is a single-threaded recursive walk with no OpenMP anywhere under scripts/.
claim_reviews.concerns: If the 157s baseline was single-threaded, the headline conflates thread-count with algorithmic/GPU gain.

claim_reviews.claim: v5 verifies 1e8 in 7.5s on a single B200.
claim_reviews.evidence: No archived log. CERTIFICATE.md probe: unclipped peak frontier at max_d=1e8 is 1.91e9 (95.5% of 2e9 BUF_SLOTS), so a single-buffer run sits near the silent-failure threshold.
v6 header and CERTIFICATE.md state that num_rounds=1 runs at d<=1e9 clipped heavily; a clipped run is not a valid verification timing.

claim_reviews.claim: An 8-GPU system verifies all denominators <= 1e10 in 43 seconds (cites run_10B_v2.log).
claim_reviews.evidence: Independently confirmed: run_10B_v2.log ends Uncovered: 9443180 / Time: 43.4s. The clean verification is run_10B_v3.log: Uncovered: 0 / Time: 178.7s (~4.2x slower). Same pattern at 1e11 (243.9M uncovered in 375.9s vs 0 in 1746.3s).
claim_reviews.concerns: A headline data-block figure is refuted by the artifact the finding links as evidence.

claim_reviews.claim: Live matrix count peaks around depth 12-13 (~244M matrices).
claim_reviews.evidence: 244140625 = 5^12 is the unpruned depth-12 count, not a peak. CERTIFICATE probes show true peaks >>244M (1.91e9 at 1e8; >25e9 for num_rounds=1 at larger ranges).
claim_reviews.concerns: Wrong frontier model caused undersized single-round configurations.

claim_reviews.claim: Clean large-d coverage runs exist and are trustworthy as one-sided certificates when Uncovered:0.
claim_reviews.evidence: run_10B_v3 (0/178.7s), run_100B_v2 (0/1746.3s), run_210B (0/6962.2s). Mark-before-drop implies clipping can only create false alarms, never fake a successful verification — but without v6.1 overflow certificates these remain strong evidence, not certified no-overflow proofs.

remediation_check: Prior remediations added hardware detail and hedges, but the finding still cites the failed 43s run as a successful verification; the duplicate certification block remains; CUDA/memory figures conflict with CERTIFICATE.md (12.8/192 vs 13.0/183).
missing_references: Archived logs for 1e7/1e8/1e9 v5 timings and the v4 baseline
Merrill-Garland-Grimshaw (2012) GPU graph traversal / stream compaction
Hensley bounded-CF counting for frontier growth
overall_assessment: The fused matrix-enumeration kernel is a genuine architectural advance, and the clean multipass logs legitimately reach Uncovered:0 at 1e10 (~179s), 1e11 (~1746s), and 2.1e11 (~6962s). But the published headline numbers do not survive contact with cited artifacts: the 43s "verification" left 9.44M denominators uncovered, the 14.4s/1e9 row is invalidated by clipping, and the OpenMP/224-thread baseline is contradicted by the committed single-threaded v4.c. Independent re-verification agrees with the 2026-07-21 fable deep audit on every decisive claim.
recommendations: Change verified_10B_time to 178.7s and cite run_10B_v3.log; label 43s as an invalid clipped run if retained
Strike or qualify the 1e9=14.4s row using CERTIFICATE.md
Archive 1e7/1e8 timings and correct the v4 baseline description (no OpenMP in committed code)
Remove the duplicate certification block; reconcile CUDA/HBM with CERTIFICATE.md
Document mark-before-drop one-sided soundness and re-run under v6.1 with no-overflow certificates
certification_justification: A headline data-block claim is directly refuted by the log it cites. This is an evidentiary failure, not fabricated engineering: after correcting to certified clean runs, bronze would be appropriate. Certification should be withdrawn until revision.
